bill.title: Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025
subjects: War crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity

industries.rationale: The bill creates new procedural pathways and limits defenses in civil litigation, expanding the scope and duration of claims that law firms may pursue or defend.
Museums and cultural institutions that hold or exhibit artwork are directly affected by expanded liability and procedural rules for restitution claims.
Banks and auction houses that handle art transactions or hold art as collateral face potential claims if works in their possession are subject to restitution.

bill.plainSummary: This bill removes the 2026 deadline for filing lawsuits to recover art and other property taken during Nazi persecution between 1933 and 1945. It makes it easier to sue foreign governments and defendants located anywhere in the United States, and it blocks certain legal defenses that courts have used to dismiss these claims, such as arguments that too much time has passed. The changes apply to cases already filed as well as future ones.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

bill.title: Keeping All Students Safe Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates schools and Head Start programs, imposing new training requirements, compliance procedures, and enforcement obligations on educational institutions.
The bill creates a new private right of action for students subjected to unlawful seclusion or restraint, which would generate litigation opportunities.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit schools and Head Start programs that receive federal funding from using seclusion (confining a student alone in a locked room) and would restrict the use of physical restraints to situations where a student poses an imminent danger of serious physical injury. It requires staff training in crisis intervention, establishes procedures for reporting incidents, and creates enforcement mechanisms including the ability for students to sue and for federal agencies to withhold payments from programs that violate the rules. The bill also provides grants to help state education agencies implement these policies.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: Patients Deserve Price Tags Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 522.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services
Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new price-disclosure obligations on hospitals and surgical centers, changing their administrative and compliance requirements.
Medical device costs must be included in the price estimates, affecting how device manufacturers' products are priced and disclosed to patients.
Price transparency requirements may affect how insurers negotiate rates and how patients understand their coverage and out-of-pocket costs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, and other healthcare facilities to provide patients with upfront price estimates for scheduled procedures and services. The estimates would need to include costs for the facility, physicians, anesthesia, medical devices, and other associated charges. Facilities that fail to provide these price disclosures could face civil penalties.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects dairy producers and processors by expanding the types of milk schools may purchase and serve.
Schools participating in the lunch program face new training requirements and changes to meal planning and procurement rules.
Food service companies and suppliers to school meal programs would adjust product offerings to meet the expanded milk and nondairy beverage options.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow schools participating in the National School Lunch Program to offer whole milk and 2% milk to students, in addition to the low-fat and fat-free options currently required. It would expand nondairy milk alternatives, permit parents (not just doctors) to request milk substitutes for students with dietary restrictions, and exclude milk fat from saturated fat limits in school meals. The bill also requires annual food allergy training and certification for school food service staff.

districtAwards.description:
DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AWARD IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO THE PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION.  THE RECIPIENT WILL IMPLEMENT GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) REDUCTION PROGRAMS, POLICIES, PROJECTS, AND MEASURES IDENTIFIED IN THE COMMONWEALTH'S PRIORITY CLIMATE ACTION PLAN (PCAP) DEVELOPED UNDER THEIR CLIMATE POLLUTION REDUCTION GRANTS (CPRG) PLANNING GRANT. ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED THROUGH THIS GRANT WILL BENEFIT ALL RESIDENTS AND VISITORS TO THE COMMONWEALTH OF PENNSYLVANIA THROUGH FOUR MAIN OBJECTIVES: IMPLEMENTATION OF AMBITIOUS MEASURES THAT WILL ACHIEVE SIGNIFICANT CUMULATIVE GHG REDUCTIONS BY 2030 AND BEYOND; PURSUIT OF MEASURES THAT WILL ACHIEVE SUBSTANTIAL COMMUNITY BENEFITS, PARTICULARLY IN LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES; COMPLEMENTING OTHER FUNDING SOURCES TO MAXIMIZE THESE GHG REDUCTIONS AND COMMUNITY BENEFITS; AND, PURSUIT OF INNOVATIVE POLICIES AND PROGRAMS THAT ARE REPLICABLE AND CAN BE 'SCALED UP' ACROSS MULTIPLE JURISDICTIONS. ACTIVITIES:PENNSYLVANIA WILL CONDUCT ITS OWN SUBAWARD COMPETITION TO RE-EQUIP ANY INDUSTRIAL OR MANUFACTURING FACILITY WITH EQUIPMENT DESIGNED TO REDUCE GHG EMISSIONS. SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OF THE SUBAWARDEES WILL INCLUDE: ELECTRIFICATION TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS LOW- OR ZERO-CARBON PROCESS HEAT SYSTEMS, ELECTRIC HEAT PUMPS, COMBINED HEAT AND POWER (CHP) SYSTEMS, THERMAL STORAGE, AND OTHER HEATING SYSTEMS BASED ON ELECTRICITY, CLEAN HYDROGEN, BIOMASS, OR WASTE HEAT RECOVERY; ENERGY EFFICIENCY TECHNOLOGIES THOSE THAT REDUCE DIRECT FUEL OR ELECTRICITY USE, UTILIZE INSULATION, SENSORS, OR CONTROLS OR DEPLOY SMART ENERGY MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS OR OTHER ADVANCED ENERGY EFFICIENCY TECHNOLOGIES; INDUSTRIAL PROCESS EMISSIONS AND WASTE REDUCTION TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS THOSE THAT REDUCE WASTE IN INDUSTRIAL APPLICATIONS, INCLUDING INDUSTRIAL HEAT PUMPS, CHP SYSTEMS, OR ADVANCED RECYCLING APPROACHES; FUEL SWITCHING TECHNOLOGIES THAT ENABLE THE TRANSITION TO LOW CARBON FUELS SUCH AS FLUIDIZED BED BIOMASS FURNACES, SOLAR-THERMAL HEATING SYSTEMS, AND DIRECT REDUCED IRON SHAFT FURNACES DESIGNED OR RETROFITTED FOR HYDROGEN-BASED REDUCTION; ON-SITE RENEWABLE ENERGY TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEMS, WIND TURBINES, MICRO-HYDROPOWER, OR GEOTHERMAL; CARBON CAPTURE, UTILIZATION, AND STORAGE (CCUS) TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS FLUE GAS CARBON CAPTURE SYSTEMS OR CALCIUM LOOPING CO2 CAPTURE SYSTEMS; FUGITIVE EMISSIONS REDUCTION TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS REGENERATIVE THERMAL OXIDIZERS AND VENTILATION AIR SYSTEMS; AND ANY OTHER TECHNOLOGY THAT REDUCES INDUSTRIAL GHG EMISSIONS, AS DETERMINED BY DEP. 
SUBRECIPIENT:SMALL-, MEDIUM- AND LARGE-SCALE GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS REDUCTION PROJECTS FOR INDUSTRIAL DECARBONZATION WILL BE COMPETITIVELY AWARDED EITHER DIRECTLY BY PADEP OR BY ITS SUBRECIPIENT PENNTAP. 
OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE: STANDING UP A STATEWIDE INDUSTRIAL DECARBONIZATION GRANT PROGRAM; COMPLETING 100-1,657 SMALL-SCALE PROJECTS, 5-50 MEDIUM-SCALE PROJECTS, AND 1-7 LARGE-SCALE PROJECTS; REDUCING AIR POLLUTANTS INCLUDING CAPS AND HAPS THROUGHOUT PENNSYLVANIA AND IN LOW INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES (LIDACS); SUBMISSION OF COMMUNITY BENEFITS PLANS (CBPS); AND PUBLISHING AN INDUSTRIAL DECARBONIZATION PLAYBOOK WITH CASE STUDIES DESCRIBING SUCCESSFUL PROJECTS. 

THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE: REDUCTION IN CUMULATIVE METRIC TONS OF GHG EMISSIONS, INCLUDING 4,332,303 METRIC TONS CO2E FROM 2025-2030 AND 8,047,294 METRIC TONS CO2E FROM 2025-2050; REDUCTION IN ANNUAL CRITERIA AIR POLLUTANTS, INCLUDING PARTICULATE MATTER (BOTH PM2.5 AND PM10), CARBON MONOXIDE, SULFUR DIOXIDE, OZONE, AND NITROGEN DIOXIDE, AND HAZARDOUS AIR POLLUTANTS, INCLUDING HYDROGEN SULFIDE, BENZENE, TOLUENE, ETHYLBENZENE,  XYLENE, HEXANE, ETHANE, PENTANE, FORMALDEHYDE, BUTANE, DICHLOROBENZENE, AND PROPANE, IN LIDACS IN 2030; LOWER ENERGY DEMAND AND INDUSTRIAL ENERGY EXPENDITURES; ENHANCED LEVEL OF COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT; CREATION OF HIGH-QUALITY JOBS; AND REDUCI
